English R1B · Reading and Composition

Micrographia (Selections)

《显微图谱》节选 · 前言与三项观察

Robert Hooke

1665前言 + Observation I / XXVI / LIV逐段对照

罗伯特·胡克，Micrographia（《显微图谱》，1665）节选：前言，及观察一（针尖）、观察二十六（痒的成因）、观察五十四（虱子）。原书图版（Schemes / Figures）未收入，文中 A、B、CC、FFF 等标记均指原图中的部位。引用与作业请以英文原文为准。

Preface前⾔

It is the great prerogative of Mankind above other Creatures, that we are not only able to behold the works of Nature, or barely to sustein our lives by them, but we have also the power of considering, comparing, altering, assisting, and improving them to various uses. And as this is the peculiar priviledge of humane Nature in general, so is it capable of being so far advanced by the helps of Art, and Experience, as to make some Men excel others in their Observations, and Deductions, almost as much as they do Beasts. By the addition of such artificial Instruments and methods, there may be, in some manner, a reparation made for the mischiefs, and imperfection, mankind has drawn upon it self, by negligence, and intemperance, and a wilful and superstitious deserting the Prescripts and Rules of Nature, whereby every man, both from a deriv’d corruption, innate and born with him, and from his breeding and converse with men, is very subject to slip into all sorts of errors.

⼈类⾼于其他造物的⼀⼤特权，在于我们不仅能够观看⾃然的作品，或仅仅依靠它们维持⽣命，我们还拥有思考、⽐较、改动、辅助并将其改良以供各种⽤途的能⼒。这既是⼈性所 独有的特权，⽽借助技艺与经验，它⼜能被提升到如此地步，以致某些⼈在观察与推论上胜过他⼈，其差距之⼤，⼏乎不亚于⼈胜过禽兽。凭借这类⼈造的仪器与⽅法，⼈类因疏忽、放 纵，以及固执⽽迷信地背弃⾃然的规诫与法则⽽⾃招的祸害与缺陷，或许可以在某种程度上得到修补；正是由于这种背弃，每个⼈——既因与⽣俱来、承袭⽽得的败坏，也因其教养与⼈ 际交往——都极易滑⼊种种谬误。

The only way which now remains for us to recover some degree of those former perfections, seems to be, by rectifying the operations of the Sense, the Memory, and Reason, since upon the evidence, the strength, the integrity, and the right correspondence of all these, all the light, by which our actions are to be guided is to be renewed, and all our command over things is to be establisht.

如今留给我们、可⽤以重新获得⼏分昔⽇完善的唯⼀途径，似乎就是矫正感官、记忆与理性的运作；因为唯有依靠这三者的确证、⼒量、完整以及彼此之间的正确呼应，那指引我们 ⾏动的⼀切光亮才能被重新点燃，我们对万物的⽀配也才能得以确⽴。

Observation I: Of the point of a sharp small needle观察⼀：论细针的针尖

As in Geometry, the most natural way of beginning is from a Mathematical point; so is the same method in Observations and Natural history the most genuine, simple, and instructive. We must first endevour to make letters, and draw single strokes true, before we venture to write whole Sentences, or to draw large Pictures. And in Physical Enquiries, we must endevour to follow Nature in the more plain and easie ways she treads in the most simple and uncompounded bodies, to trace her steps, and be acquainted with her manner of walking there, before we venture our selves into the multitude of meanders she has in bodies of a more complicated nature; lest, being unable to distinguish and judge of our way, we quickly lose both Nature our Guide, and our selves too, and are left to wander in the labyrinth of groundless opinions; wanting both judgment, that light, and experience, that clew, which should direct our proceedings.

正如在⼏何学中，最⾃然的开端是从⼀个数学上的点开始；在观察与博物志中，同样的⽅法也最为本真、最为简单、最富教益。我们必须先努⼒把字⺟写好、把每⼀笔单独的笔画画 准，然后才敢去写整句话，或去画⼤幅的图。在物理探究中，我们也必须先在最简单、最未经复合的物体上，沿着⾃然所⾛的那些较为平坦易⾏的道路去跟随她，追踪她的步伐，熟悉她 在那⾥⾏⾛的⽅式，然后才敢让⾃⼰踏⼊她在更为复杂的物体中所布下的重重曲径；否则，⼀旦⽆法辨认和判断道路，我们就会很快既失去我们的向导⾃然，也失去我们⾃⼰，只能在毫 ⽆根据的意⻅所构成的迷宫中徘徊，既没有判断⼒这盏灯，也没有经验这根引线来指引我们前⾏。

We will begin these our Inquiries therefore with the Observations of Bodies of the most simple nature first, and so gradually proceed to those of a more compounded one. In prosecution of which method, we shall begin with a Physical point; of which kind the Point of a Needle is commonly reckon’d for one; and is indeed, for the most part, made so sharp, that the naked eye cannot distinguish any parts of it: It very easily pierces, and makes its way through all kind of bodies softer then it self: But if view’d with a very good Microscope, we may find that the top of a Needle (though as to the sense very sharp) appears a broad, blunt, and very irregular end; not resembling a Cone, as is imagin’d, but onely a piece of a tapering body, with a great part of the top remov’d, or deficient. The Points of Pins are yet more blunt, and the Points of the most curious Mathematical Instruments do very seldome arrive at so great a sharpness; how much therefore can be built upon demonstrations made onely by the productions of the Ruler and Compasses, he will be better able to consider that shall but view those points and lines with a Microscope.

因此，我们将从对性质最简单的物体的观察⼊⼿，再逐步推进到更为复合的物体。依此⽅法，我们先从⼀个物理意义上的点开始；针尖通常就被算作这样⼀种点，⽽且它多半确实做 得极尖，以致⾁眼分辨不出它的任何部分：它极容易刺⼊并穿过⼀切⽐它柔软的物体。然⽽若⽤⼀架很好的显微镜来看，我们会发现针的顶端（尽管对感官⽽⾔极尖）呈现为⼀个宽阔、 钝拙⽽极不规则的末端；它并不像⼈们想象的那样是⼀个圆锥，⽽不过是⼀段渐细物体的残余，其顶端有很⼤⼀部分被磨去或残缺。别针的尖端更钝，就连最精致的数学仪器的尖端也极 少能达到如此的锐利程度；由此，仅凭直尺与圆规所作出的证明究竟能承载多少东西，凡是肯⽤显微镜看⼀看那些点与线的⼈，都会更有能⼒去掂量。

Now though this point be commonly accounted the sharpest (whence when we would express the sharpness of a point the most superlatively, we say, As sharp as a Needle) yet the Microscope can afford us hundreds of Instances of Points many thousand times sharper: such as those of the hairs, and bristles, and claws of multitudes of Insects; the thorns, or crooks, or hairs of leaves, and other small vegetables; nay, the ends of the stiriæ or small parallelipipeds of Amianthus, and alumen plumosum; of many of which, though the Points are so sharp as not to be visible, though view’d with a Microscope (which magnifies the Object, in bulk, above a million of times) yet I doubt not, but were we able practically to make Microscopes according to the theory of them, we might find hills, and dales, and pores, and a sufficient bredth, or expansion, to give all those parts elbow-room, even in the blunt top of the very Point of any of these so very sharp bodies.

如今，尽管这种针尖被公认为最尖（因此我们要极⾔⼀物之尖时，便说“尖如针”），显微镜却能给我们提供成百上千个⽐它尖锐千百倍的例⼦：譬如⽆数昆⾍的⽑、鬃与⽖；叶⽚ 与其他⼩植物的刺、钩或茸⽑；甚⾄⽯棉与⽻状明矾那些针状晶体或细⼩平⾏六⾯体的端头。其中许多的尖端已尖到即便⽤显微镜（其放⼤物体的体积在百万倍以上）也看不⻅的地步； 然⽽我毫不怀疑，倘若我们真能按照显微镜的理论把它造出来，那么即便在这些极尖之物的尖端那钝拙的顶部，我们也会发现丘陵、⾕地与孔隙，以及⾜够的宽度或展开空间，让所有那 些部分都有回旋的余地。

For certainly the quantity or extension of any body may be Divisible in infinitum, though perhaps not the matter.

因为任何物体的量或⼴延必定可以⽆限分割，尽管物质或许并⾮如此。

But to proceed: The Image we have here exhibited in the first Figure, was the top of a small and very sharp Needle, whose point aa nevertheless appear’d through the Microscope above a quarter of an inch broad, not round nor flat, but irregular and uneven; so that it seem’d to have been big enough to have afforded a hundred armed Mites room enough to be rang’d by each other without endangering the breaking one anothers necks, by being thrust off on either side. The surface of which, though appearing to the naked eye very smooth, could not nevertheless hide a multitude of holes and scratches and ruggednesses from being discover’d by the Microscope to invest it, several of which inequalities (as A, B, C, seem’d holes made by some small specks of Rust; and D some adventitious body, that stuck very close to it) were casual. All the rest that roughen the surface, were onely so many marks of the rudeness and bungling of Art.

再往下说：我们在第⼀幅图中所展⽰的影像，是⼀枚细⼩⽽极尖的针的顶端；然⽽它的尖端 aa 在显微镜下看去竟有四分之⼀英⼨多宽，既不圆也不平，⽽是不规则、坑洼不平；以致 它似乎⼤得⾜以容纳⼀百只披甲的螨⾍并排列队，彼此挤在⼀起也不⾄于把对⽅推下去⽽摔断脖⼦。它的表⾯在⾁眼看来虽极光滑，却仍⽆法掩藏那许多被显微镜发现的、遍布其上的孔 洞、划痕与凹凸；其中若⼲处不平（如 A、B、C 似乎是⼏点⼩锈斑蚀出的孔洞，⽽ D 则是某个偶然附着、紧贴其上的外来物）纯属偶然。⾄于其余⼀切使表⾯变得粗糙的东西，则不过 是技艺之粗劣与笨拙留下的道道痕迹罢了。

So unaccurate is it, in all its productions, even in those which seem most neat, that if examin’d with an organ more acute then that by which they were made, the more we see of their shape, the less appearance will there be of their beauty: whereas in the works of Nature, the deepest Discoveries shew us the greatest Excellencies. An evident Argument, that he that was the Author of all these things, was no other then Omnipotent; being able to include as great a variety of parts and contrivances in the yet smallest Discernable Point, as in those vaster bodies (which comparatively are called also Points) such as the Earth, Sun, or Planets. Nor need it seem strange that the Earth it self may be by an Analogie call’d a Physical Point: For as its body, though now so near us as to fill our eys and fancies with a sense of the vastness of it, may by a little Distance, and some convenient Diminishing Glasses, be made vanish into a scarce visible Speck, or Point (as I have often try’d on the Moon, and (when not too bright) on the Sun it self.) So, could a Mechanical contrivance succesfully answer our Theory, we might see the least spot as big as the Earth it self; and Discover, as Des Cartes also conjectures (Diop. ch. 10. § 9.), as great a variety of bodies in the Moon, or Planets, as in the Earth.

技艺在它的⼀切制品中——哪怕是那些看上去最⼯整的制品——都如此不精确，以致若⽤⼀种⽐制造它们时所⽤的更为敏锐的器官去检视，我们对其形状看得越多，它的美就越发⽆从 显现；反之，在⾃然的作品中，越是深⼊的发现，越是向我们展⽰出最⼤的精妙。这有⼒地表明：那创造这⼀切之物的作者不是别的，正是全能者；因为他能够在最⼩的可⻅之点中，容 纳与那些更为巨⼤的物体（相较之下它们也被称作点），如地球、太阳或⾏星之中同样丰富多样的部分与构造。地球本⾝可以由类⽐⽽被称为⼀个物理之点，这也不必显得奇怪：因为它 的形体虽如今离我们如此之近，以致充满我们的眼睛与想象，使我们感到它的浩⼤，但只要略微拉开距离，再借助某些合适的缩⼩镜，就能使它化为⼀个⼏乎看不⻅的斑点或点（我常常 对⽉亮这样试验过，在光不太强时也对太阳本⾝试过）。同样，倘若某种机械装置能够成功地实现我们的理论，我们或许就能把最⼩的斑点看得如地球那么⼤；并且如笛卡⼉所推测的那 样（《屈光学》第⼗章第九节），在⽉亮或⾏星上发现与地球上同样丰富多样的物体。

But leaving these Discoveries to future Industries, we shall proceed to add one Observation more of a point commonly so call’d, that is, the mark of a full stop, or period. And for this purpose I observed many both printed ones and written; and among multitudes I found few of them more round or

但把这些发现留给⽇后的努⼒吧。我们接着再补充⼀项对通常所谓“点”的观察，也就是句号或句点这个符号。为此我观察了许多印刷的和⼿写的句点；在众多之中，我发现⽐我在 第⼆图版第三幅图中所描画的这⼀个更圆或更

regular then this which I have delineated in the third figure of the second Scheme, but very many abundantly more disfigur’d; and for the most part if they seem’d equally round to the eye, I found those points that had been made by a Copper-plate, and Roll-press, to be as misshapen as those which had been made with Types, the most curious and smothly engraven strokes and points, looking but as so many furrows and holes, and their printed impressions, but like smutty daubings on a matt or uneven floor with a blunt extinguisht brand or stick’s end. And as for points made with a pen they were much more ragged and deformed. Nay, having view’d certain pieces of exceeding curious writing of the kind (one of which in the bredth of a two-pence compris’d the Lords prayer, the Apostles Creed, the ten Commandments, and about half a dozen verses besides of the Bible, whose lines were so small and near together, that I was unable to number them with my naked eye,) a very ordinary Microscope, I had then about me, inabled me to see that what the Writer of it had asserted was true, but withall discover’d of what pitifull bungling scribbles and scrawls it was compos’d, Arabian and China characters being almost as well shap’d, yet thus much I must say for the Man, that it was for the most part legible enough, though in some places there wanted a good fantsy well preposest to help one through.

规整的实在很少，⽽畸形得多的却⽐⽐皆是；⽽且⼤体上说，如果它们在眼中显得同样圆，我发现由铜版和滚筒印刷机压出的点，与⽤活字排出的点⼀样⾛形——那些最精致、刻得 最光滑的笔画与圆点，看上去也不过是⼀道道沟槽和⼀个个孔洞，⽽它们印出的痕迹，则像是⽤⼀根烧秃了的⽕棍或棒头，在粗糙不平的地⾯上涂抹出的污迹。⾄于⽤笔写出的点，就更 加⽑糙变形了。不仅如此，我还看过⼏件这类极其精巧的书写作品（其中⼀件在两便⼠硬币的宽度内写下了主祷⽂、使徒信经、⼗诫，另外还有半打左右的《圣经》经⽂，其⾏距既⼩⼜ 密，我⽤⾁眼根本数不清有多少⾏）；我当时随⾝带的⼀架很普通的显微镜，使我看清了书写者所宣称的确属事实，但同时也发现它是由何等可怜、拙劣的涂鸦与潦草笔迹构成的——阿 拉伯⽂和中国⽂字的字形⼏乎都⽐它端正。不过有⼀点我必须为此⼈说句公道话：它⼤体上还算辨认得出，尽管在有些地⽅需要⼀点先⼊为主的好想象⼒才能读通。

If this manner of small writing were made easie and practicable (and I think I know such a one, but have never yet made tryal of it, whereby one might be inabled to write a great deale with much ease, and accurately enough in a very little roome) it might be of very good use to convey secret Intelligence without any danger of Discovery or mistrusting. But to come again to the point. The Irregularities of it are caused by three or four coadjutors, one of which is, the uneven surface of the paper, which at best appears no smother then a very course piece of shag’d cloth, next the irregularity of the Type or Ingraving, and a third is the rough Daubing of the Printing-Ink that lies upon the instrument that makes the impression, to all which, add the variation made by the Different lights and shadows, and you may have sufficient reason to ghess that a point may appear much more ugly then this, which I have here presented, which though it appear’d through the Microscope gray, like a great splatch of London dirt, about three inches over; yet to the naked eye it was black and no bigger then that in the midst of the Circle A.

倘若这种细⼩书写的⽅法能变得容易⽽可⾏（我想我知道⼀种，只是尚未试验过，凭它⼈们可以毫不费⼒地在极⼩的空间⾥写下⼤量⽂字，并且⾜够准确），那么它⽤来传递秘密情 报会⼤有⽤处，⽽不必担⼼被⼈发现或起疑。但还是回到“点”上来。它的不规则由三四个共同因素造成：其⼀是纸⾯的不平，纸⾯即便在最好的情况下，看上去也不⽐⼀块极粗糙的起 绒布更光滑；其次是活字或雕版本⾝的不规则；第三是压印器具上所敷印刷油墨的粗劣涂布；再加上不同光影所造成的变化——你就有充分的理由推想，⼀个点可能⽐我在此呈现的这⼀ 个还要难看得多。这个点透过显微镜看去是灰⾊的，像伦敦街上⼀⼤摊污泥，约有三英⼨宽；⽽在⾁眼看来，它却是⿊的，并且不⽐圆圈 A 正中的那个点更⼤。

And could I have found Room in this Plate to have inserted an O you should have seen that the letters were not more distinct then the points of Distinction, nor a drawn circle more exactly so, then we have now shown a point to be a point.

⽽且，我若能在这块图版上找到地⽅插⼊⼀个字⺟ O，你就会看到：字⺟并不⽐标点符号更清晰分明，⼀个画出来的圆也并不⽐我们如今所展⽰的“点之为点”更精确地是⼀个圆。

Observ. XXVI. Of Cowage, and the itching operation of some bodies.观察⼆⼗六：论刺⽑黧⾖，及某些物体致痒的作⽤

There is a certain Down of a Plant, brought from the East-Indies, call’d commonly, though very improperly, Cow-itch, the reason of which mistake is manifest enough from the description of it, which Mr. Parkinson sets down in his Herbal, Tribe XI. Chap. 2. Phasiolus siliqua hirsuta; The hairy Kidney-bean, called in Zurratte where it grows, Couhage: We have had (says he) another of this kind brought us out of the East-Indies, which being planted was in shew like the former, but came not to perfection, the unkindly season not suffering it to shew the flower; but of the Cods that were brought, some were smaller, shorter, and rounder then the Garden kind; others much longer, and many growing together, as it were in clusters, and cover’d all over with a brown short hairiness, so fine, that if any of it be rubb’d, or fall on the back of ones hand, or other tender parts of the skin, it will cause a kind of itching, but not strong, nor long induring, but passing quickly away, without either danger or harm; the Beans were smaller then ordinary, and of a black shining colour.

有⼀种从东印度带来的植物茸⽑，通称“⽜痒”（Cow-itch），不过这个名称很不恰当；这⼀误称的缘由，从帕⾦森先⽣在其《本草》第⼗⼀族第⼆章中的描述⾥已⾜够清楚：

Phasiolus siliqua hirsuta，即多⽑的菜⾖，在其⽣⻓地苏拉特被称为 Couhage。他说：我们曾从东印度得到过这⼀类的另⼀种，种下之后外观与前⼀种相似，却未能⻓成，因为时令不

佳，不容它开花；但在带来的⾖荚中，有些⽐园中所种的更⼩、更短、更圆，另⼀些则⻓得多，并且许多聚⽣在⼀起，仿佛成簇，通体覆盖着褐⾊的短茸⽑，细到只要有⼀点被擦到，或 落在⼈的⼿背或⽪肤其他柔嫩的部位，就会引起⼀种痒，但既不强烈，也不持久，很快就过去了，既⽆危险也⽆伤害；⾖⼦⽐寻常的⼩，呈⿊⽽有光泽的颜⾊。

Having one of these Cods given me by a Sea-Captain, who had frequented those parts, I found it to be a small Cod, about three Inches long, much like a short Cod of French Beans, which had six Beans in it, the whole surface of it was cover’d over with a very thick and shining brown Down or Hair, which was very fine, and for its bigness stiff; taking some of this Down, and rubbing it on the back of my hand, I found very little or no trouble, only I was sensible that several of these little downy parts with rubbing did penetrate, and were sunk, or stuck pretty deep into my skin. After I had thus rubb’d it for a pretty while, I felt very little or no pain, in so much that I doubted, whether it were the true Couhage; but whil’st I was considering; I found the Down begin to make my hand itch, and in some places to smart again, much like the stinging of a Flea or Gnat, and this continued a pretty while, so that by degrees I found my skin to be swell’d with little red pustules, and to look as if it had been itchie.

⼀位常来往于那⼀带的船⻓送了我⼀个这样的⾖荚。我发现它是个⼩荚，约三英⼨⻓，很像⼀段短的四季⾖荚，⾥⾯有六粒⾖⼦；它的整个表⾯覆盖着极稠密⽽有光泽的褐⾊茸⽑， 这些⽑⾮常细，但就其⼤⼩⽽⾔相当硬。我取了⼀些茸⽑，在⼿背上摩擦，发现⼏乎没有什么不适，只是能感觉到有⼏根细⼩的绒⽑随着摩擦刺⼊，并陷进或扎得相当深地留在我的⽪肤 ⾥。这样擦了好⼀会⼉之后，我⼏乎感觉不到疼痛，以致我怀疑这是否真是 Couhage；但正当我思忖之际，我发现那茸⽑开始使我的⼿发痒，有些地⽅⼜刺痛起来，很像被跳蚤或蚊蚋叮 咬，这样持续了好⼀阵，于是我渐渐发现⽪肤上肿起⼀个个⼩红疹，看上去就像发过痒似的。

But suffering it without rubbing or scratching, the itching tickling pain quickly grew languid, and within an hour I felt nothing at all, and the little protuberancies were vanish’d.

但我忍着不去揉搓或抓挠，那种⼜痒⼜刺的疼痛很快就变得微弱，不到⼀⼩时我便什么也感觉不到了，那些⼩⼩的凸起也消失了。

The cause of which odd Phænomenon, I suppose to be much the same with that of the stinging of a Nettle, for by the Microscope, I discover’d this Down to consist of a multitude of small and slender conical bodies, much resembling Needles or Bodkins, such as are represented by AB. CD. EF. of the first Figure of the XVI. Scheme; that their ends AAA, were very sharp, and the substance of them stiff and hard, much like the substance of several kinds of Thorns and crooks growing on Trees. And though they appear’d very cleer and transparent, yet I could not perceive whether they were hollow or not, but to me they appear’d like solid transparent bodies, without any cavity in them; whether, though they might not be a kind of Cane, fill’d with some transparent liquor which was hardned (because the Cod which I had was very dry) I was not able to examine.

这⼀奇特现象的成因，我想与荨⿇蜇⼈的成因⼤致相同；因为借助显微镜，我发现这种茸⽑是由⽆数细⼩⽽纤⻓的锥状体构成的，很像针或锥⼦，即第⼗六图版第⼀幅图中 AB、

CD、EF 所表⽰的那样；它们的末端 AAA 极为尖锐，其质地坚硬挺实，很像树上所⽣的⼏种棘刺与钩芒的质地。它们虽然看上去⼗分清亮透明，我却⽆法辨明其中是否中空；在我看来它

们像是实⼼的透明体，内部并⽆空腔。⾄于它们是否可能是⼀种细管，内充某种已经硬化的透明液体（因为我得到的那个⾖荚很⼲），我则⽆从查验。

Now, being such stiff, sharp bodies, it is easie to conceive, how with rubbing they might easily be thrust into the tender parts of the skin, and there, by reason of their exceeding fineness and driness, not create any considerable trouble or pain, till by remaining in those places moistned with the humours of the body, some caustick part sticking on them, or residing within them might be dissolv’d and mix’d with the ambient juices of that place, and thereby those fibres and tender parts adjoyning become affected, and as it were corroded by it; whence, while that action lasts, the pains created are pretty sharp and pungent, though small, which is the essential property of an itching one.

既然它们是这般坚硬尖锐的物体，就不难设想：经摩擦它们很容易被推⼊⽪肤的柔嫩部位，⽽由于它们极其纤细⼲燥，起初并不会造成什么明显的不适或疼痛；直到它们留在那些被 体液润湿的地⽅，附着其上或藏于其内的某种腐蚀性成分被溶解，并与该处周围的汁液相混，于是邻近的纤维与柔嫩部分便受到侵袭，仿佛被它蚀咬；因此，在这⼀作⽤持续期间，所产 ⽣的疼痛相当尖锐刺⼈，虽然细微——⽽这正是“痒”的本质特征。

That the pain also caused by the stinging of a Flea, a Gnat, a Flie, a Wasp, and the like, proceeds much from the very same cause, I elsewhere in their proper places endeavour to manifest. The stinging also of shred Hors-hair, which in meriment is often strew’d between the sheets of a Bed, seems to proceed from the same cause.

⾄于跳蚤、蚊蚋、苍蝇、⻩蜂之类叮蜇所造成的疼痛，其成因⼤体相同，我将在别处相应的地⽅设法加以说明。此外，⼈们常常出于戏弄⽽撒在床单之间的碎⻢鬃所引起的刺痒，看 来也出于同样的原因。

Observ. LIV. Of a Louse观察五⼗四：论虱

This is a Creature so officious, that ’twill be known to every one at one time or other, so busie, and so impudent, that it will be intruding it self in every ones company, and so proud and aspiring withall, that it fears not to trample on the best, and affects nothing so much as a Crown; feeds and lives very high, and that makes it so saucy, as to pull any one by the ears that comes in its way, and will never be quiet till it has drawn blood: it is troubled at nothing so much as at a man that scratches his head, as knowing that man is plotting and contriving some mischief against it, and that makes it oftentime sculk into some meaner and lower place, and run behind a mans back, though it go very much against the hair; which ill conditions of it having made it better known then trusted, would exempt me from making any further description of it, did not my faithful Mercury, my Microscope, bring me other information of it.

这是⼀种极其殷勤多事的⽣物，⼈⼈迟早都会认识它；它如此忙碌、如此厚颜，以致要挤进每个⼈的交际圈；⽽且如此骄傲、如此有野⼼，以致敢于践踏最尊贵的⼈，最钟爱的莫过 于王冠；它吃得好、过得阔⽓，这使它如此放肆，凡挡在它路上的⼈它都要揪⼀揪耳朵，不⻅⾎决不罢休。最令它烦恼的莫过于⼀个搔头的⼈，因为它知道此⼈正在密谋算计它；这常使 它溜进某个更卑下低微的⻆落，逃到⼈的背后去，尽管那是⼤⼤地逆着⽑⽽⾏。它这些恶劣品性使它“名声在外”却不为⼈所信任，本来我尽可以免去对它的进⼀步描述——若不是我那 忠实的墨丘利、我的显微镜，给我带来了关于它的另⼀番消息的话。

For this has discovered to me, by means of a very bright light cast on it, that it is a Creature of a very odd shape; it has a head shap’d like that exprest in 35. Scheme marked with A, which seems almost Conical, but is a little flatted on the upper and under sides, at the biggest part of which, on either side behind the head (as it were, being the place where other Creatures ears stand) are placed its two black shining goggle eyes BB, looking backwards, and fenced round with several small cilia, or hairs that incompass it, so that it seems this Creature has no very good foresight: It does not seem to have any eye-lids, and therefore perhaps its eyes were so placed, that it might the better cleanse them with its fore-legs; and perhaps this may be the reason, why they so much avoid and run from the light behind them, for being made to live in the shady and dark recesses of the hair, and thence probably their eye having a great aperture, the open and clear light, especially that of the Sun, must needs very much offend them; to secure these eyes from receiving any injury from the hairs through which it passes, it has two horns that grow before it, in the place where one would have thought the eyes should be; each of these CC hath four joynts, which are fringed, as ’twere, with small brisles, from which to the tip of its snout D, the head seems very round and tapering, ending in a very sharp nose D, which seems to have a small hole, and to be the passage through which he sucks the blood.

因为借助投射在它⾝上的⼀道极亮的光，显微镜向我揭⽰出：这是⼀种形状⼗分古怪的⽣物。它的头如第三⼗五图版中标为 A 的那样，近乎圆锥形，只是上下两⾯略扁；在头部最宽 处的两侧、脑后（也就是其他动物⻓耳朵的位置），⽣着它那两只乌⿊发亮的凸眼 BB，向后望着，四周围有若⼲细⼩的纤⽑环绕，因此看来这⽣物的“前瞻”并不太好。它似乎没有眼 睑，所以它的眼睛或许⽣在那样的位置，是为了便于⽤前⾜来清洁它们；这⼤概也是它们何以如此躲避、逃离⾝后光线的缘故——因为它们⽣来就住在⽑发浓密幽暗的深处，眼睛的瞳孔 想必很⼤，敞亮清明的光线，尤其是⽇光，必定令它们极为难受。为了保护这双眼睛不被它穿⾏其间的⽑发所伤，它前⽅⻓着两只触⻆，恰在⼈们以为该⻓眼睛的地⽅；每只触⻆ CC 有 四节，节上仿佛缀着细⼩的刚⽑；从触⻆到它吻端 D 之间，头部显得很圆⽽渐细，末端是⼀个极尖的喙 D，喙上似乎有个⼩孔，即它吸⾎所经的通道。

Now whereas if it be plac’d on its back, with its belly upwards, as it is in the 35. Scheme, it seems in several Positions to have a resemblance of chaps, or jaws, as is represented in the Figure by EE, yet in other postures those dark strokes disappear; and having kept several of them in a box for two or three dayes, so that for all that time they had nothing to feed on, I found, upon letting one creep on my hand, that it immediately fell to sucking, and did neither seem to thrust its nose very deep into the skin, nor to open any kind of mouth, but I could plainly perceive a small current of blood, which came directly from its snout, and past into its belly; and about A there seem’d a contrivance, somewhat resembling a Pump, pair of Bellows, or Heart, for by a very swift systole and diastole the blood seem’d drawn from the nose, and forced into the body.

再者，若把它仰⾯放置、腹部朝上，如第三⼗五图版所⽰，在某些⻆度下它似乎有类似颊或颚的构造，即图中 EE 所表⽰者；但换成别的姿态，那些暗⾊的纹路⼜不⻅了。我曾把⼏ 只这样的⾍⼦放在盒中养了两三天，使它们在这段时间⾥⽆物可⻝；后来我让其中⼀只爬到我⼿上，发现它⽴刻吸吮起来，既不⻅把喙很深地刺⼊⽪肤，也不⻅张开任何形式的⼝，但我 能清楚地看⻅⼀⼩股⾎流，径直从它的喙进⼊它的腹部；在 A 附近似乎有⼀个装置，略像⼀台唧筒、⼀副⻛箱或⼀颗⼼脏，因为⾎液仿佛正是靠着极迅速的收缩与舒张，从喙中被吸取并 压送进体内。

It did not seem at all, though I viewed it a good while as it was sucking, to thrust more of its nose into the skin then the very snout D, nor did it cause the least discernable pain, and yet the blood seem’d to run through its head very quick and freely, so that it seems there is no part of the skin but the blood is dispers’d into, nay, even into the cuticula; for had it thrust its whole nose in from D to CC, it would not have amounted to the supposed thickness of that tegument, the length of the nose being not more then a three hundredth part of an inch. It has six legs, covered with a very transparent shell, and joynted exactly like a Crab’s, or Lobster’s; each leg is divided into six parts by these joynts, and those have here and there several small hairs; and at the end of each leg it has two claws, very properly adapted for its peculiar use, being thereby inabled to walk very securely both on the skin and hair; and indeed this contrivance of the feet is very curious, and could not be made more commodiously and compendiously, for performing both these requisite motions, of walking and climbing up the hair of a mans head, then it is: for, by having the lesser claw (a) set so much short of the bigger (b) when it walks on the skin the shorter touches not, and then the feet are the same with those of a Mite, and several other small Insects, but by means of the small joynts of the longer claw it can bend it round, and so with both claws take hold of a hair, in the manner represented in the Figure, the long transparent Cylinder FFF, being a Man’s hair held by it.

尽管我在它吸吮时看了好⼀会⼉，却始终不⻅它把喙刺⼊⽪肤的部分超出喙尖 D，也不曾引起丝毫可察觉的疼痛；然⽽⾎液似乎极快⽽顺畅地流过它的头部。由此看来，⽪肤中没有 哪⼀部分不曾有⾎液散布其间，甚⾄连表⽪也是如此；因为即便它把整个喙从 D ⼀直刺到 CC，也达不到⼈们所设想的那层表⽪的厚度，⽽喙的⻓度不过三百分之⼀英⼨。它有六条腿， 覆着⼀层极透明的甲壳，关节的构造与蟹或⻰虾的完全⼀样；每条腿被这些关节分为六段，其上零星⽣有若⼲细⽑；每条腿的末端有两只⽖，极其恰当地适应了它特有的⽤途，因⽽使它 ⽆论在⽪肤上还是⽑发上都能⾏⾛得⼗分稳当。这⾜部的构造确实⾮常精巧：要同时完成⾏⾛与攀爬⼈头发这两种必需的动作，再也没有⽐它更便利、更简省的做法了。因为较⼩的那只 ⽖ (a) ⽐较⼤的那只 (b) 短出许多，所以当它在⽪肤上⾏⾛时，短⽖并不触地，此时它的⾜与螨以及其他若⼲⼩昆⾍的⾜⽆异；⽽借助⻓⽖上的⼩关节，它⼜能把⻓⽖弯成圆形，从⽽⽤两 ⽖合抱住⼀根⽑发，正如图中所⽰——那根⻓⽽透明的圆柱 FFF，便是它所抓住的⼀根⼈的头发。

The Thorax seem’d cas’d with another kind of substance then the belly, namely, with a thin transparent horny substance, which upon the fasting of the Creature did not grow flaccid; through this I could plainly see the blood, suck’d from my hand, to be variously distributed, and mov’d to and fro; and about G there seem’d a pretty big white substance, which seem’d to be moved within its thorax; besides, there appear’d very many small milk-white vessels, which crost over the breast between the legs, out of which, on either side, were many small branchings, these seem’d to be the veins and arteries, for that which is analogus to blood in all Insects is milk-white.

胸部所包覆的物质似乎与腹部不同，是⼀层薄⽽透明的⻆质；这层⻆质在⾍⼦禁⻝时并不变得松瘪。透过它，我能清楚地看⻅从我⼿上吸去的⾎在体内四处分布、来回流动；在 G 附 近似乎有⼀团相当⼤的⽩⾊物质，看上去在胸腔内移动着。此外还显现出许多细⼩的乳⽩⾊管道，横贯双腿之间的胸部，从其两侧⼜分出许多细⼩的分⽀；这些看来就是它的静脉与动 脉，因为在⼀切昆⾍体内相当于⾎液的东西都是乳⽩⾊的。

The belly is covered with a transparent substance likewise, but more resembling a skin then a shell, for ’tis grain’d all over the belly just like the skin in the palms of a man’s hand, and when the belly is empty, grows very flaccid and wrinkled; at the upper end of this is placed the stomach HH, and perhaps also the white spot II may be the liver or pancreas, which, by the peristalick motion of the guts, is a little mov’d to and fro, not with a systole and diastole, but rather with a thronging or justling motion. Viewing one of these Creatures, after it had fasted two dayes, all the hinder part was lank and flaccid, and the white spot II hardly mov’d, most of the white branchings disappear’d, and most also of the redness or sucked blood in the guts, the peristaltick motion of which was scarce discernable; but upon the suffering it to suck, it presently fill’d the skin of the belly, and of the six scolop’d embosments on either side, as full as it could be stuft, the stomach and guts were as full as they could hold; the peristaltick motion of the gut grew quick, and the justling motion of II accordingly; multitudes of milk-white vessels seem’d quickly filled, and turgid, which were perhaps the veins and arteries and the Creature was so greedy, that though it could not contain more, yet it continued sucking as fast as ever, and as fast emptying it self behind: the digestion of this Creature must needs be very quick, for though I perceiv’d the blood thicker and blacker when suck’d, yet, when in the guts, it was of a very lovely ruby colour, and that part of it, which was digested into the veins, seemed white; whence it appears, that a further digestion of blood may make it milk, at least of a resembling colour:

腹部同样覆着⼀层透明的物质，但更像⽪⽽不像壳，因为整个腹部都布满纹理，正如⼈⼿掌上的⽪肤⼀般；当腹中空虚时，它就变得⼗分松弛⽽皱缩。腹的上端是胃 HH，⽽那个⽩ 斑 II 或许是肝或胰，它随着肠的蠕动⽽略微来回移动，不是以收缩与舒张的⽅式，⽽更像是⼀种拥挤推搡的运动。我观察其中⼀只禁⻝两天之后的⾍⼦：整个后半⾝⼲瘪松弛，⽩斑 II ⼏ 乎不动，⼤部分⽩⾊分⽀管道都消失了，肠中吸来的⾎的红⾊也⼤半消失，其蠕动⼏乎难以辨认；但⼀让它吸⾎，它⽴刻就把腹部的⽪以及两侧那六个扇⻉状的隆起撑得再也塞不下，胃 与肠也满到不能再满；肠的蠕动变快，II 的推搡运动也随之加快；⽆数乳⽩⾊的管道似乎迅速被充满⽽胀起，它们或许就是静脉与动脉。这⽣物如此贪婪，虽然已经再也容纳不下，却仍 旧照旧⻜快地吸吮，同时⼜⻜快地从后端排空⾃⼰。它的消化必定极为迅速，因为⾎在被吸⼊时我看它较浓较⿊，可⼀到肠中，却呈现出⼀种⼗分可爱的红宝⽯⾊；⽽其中被消化⼊静脉 的那⼀部分，看上去是⽩⾊的。由此看来，⾎液经过进⼀步的消化或许可以变成乳汁，⾄少在颜⾊上相似。

What is else observable in the figure of this Creature, may be seen by the 35. Scheme.

这⽣物形体上其余值得注意之处，可参⻅第三⼗五图版。
